subject.title: Workboard: improve stacked-card readability and human-approval visibility

question: Should Workboard represent approval-needed or human-action-required cards as a first-class UI signal, a configurable prominent-label rule, or leave this to existing blocked status and labels?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable product contract is not: the fix could be a UI-only affordance, a metadata/status convention, or a new plugin config surface, and repository policy sets a high bar for new config/default behavior.

options.title: Use existing signals
options.body: Add a UI-local human-action or approval affordance from existing status, labels, notes, or metadata without adding plugin config unless a later gap requires it.

options.title: Add configurable labels
options.body: Define a plugin-owned config contract for prominent approval label patterns, with docs and tests for the new user-visible config surface.

options.title: Document current workflow
options.body: Keep generic blocked status and labels as the supported path and document the convention instead of adding first-class approval UX now.

recommendation.title: Use existing signals
recommendation.body: Add a UI-local human-action or approval affordance from existing status, labels, notes, or metadata without adding plugin config unless a later gap requires it.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the Workboard plugin and dashboard surface and has the strongest history-backed tie to the product-surface decision.
